A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching algorithms, theoretical results, experiments, and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-restoration experiments, optimizer and early-stopping ablations, failure-mode tests, and synthetic posterior-concentration results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, spatial-correlation measurements, scientific inverse problems, prior-swap controls, and noise-sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The initial-noise optimization objective, AdamSphere updates, and HoldoutTopK selection procedure remain unchanged in Section 2.1 and Appendix B. The added exponential-map formula documents an option already described in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds Linear Scattering and nonlinear Black Hole Imaging from InverseBench, substantially extending coverage beyond natural-image restoration. It also evaluates higher-noise scenarios. Existing natural-image tasks remain, while the compute comparison switches from FFHQ to CelebA-HQ.

E2.justification: Appendices C.3–C.4 add actual comparisons against DAPS and DiffPIR on inpainting, Gaussian deblurring, and 4× super-resolution, and Deep Random Projector on inpainting. The existing DPS, DMPlug, and DSG comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include 3-versus-20-step sampling with 100 unconditional samples per setting, fixed-DPS prior swaps, three receiver configurations, and blur-PSNR evaluation. The compute study replaces v1's 100-/1000-step DPS curves extending to 10,000 evaluations with a 999–5000-NFE comparison using 333/1000 INO iterations and single/best-of-three/best-of-five DPS runs. Main restoration settings are otherwise largely retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds spatial-autocorrelation diagnostics to investigate retained structure, fixed-solver prior-swap experiments to examine domain mismatch separately, and sensitivity tests over Gaussian noise levels 0.01–1.0. These substantially expand the analysis beyond v1's retained optimizer ablations and box-inpainting/super-resolution failure studies.

E5.justification: v1 reports score-gap dispersion but only point estimates for reconstruction quality. v2 adds DRP PSNR/SSIM standard deviations in Table 9 and ± quantities for Black Hole Imaging in Table 11. The latter quantities and their replication basis are not defined, so they do not establish additional seeded runs or significance testing.

E6.justification: The original benchmark values are retained after renumbering, but substantial baseline, scientific-imaging, correlation, prior-mismatch, and noise results are added. For example, Table 16 reports that at noise 1.0, DPS reaches 22.42 PSNR versus 20.52 and 16.88 for in-domain and out-of-domain INO. The replaced compute results use different data and budgets and cannot establish a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix C.8 introduces formal definitions of the distance-binned normalized autocorrelation and its sample-averaged profile, including the property Cx(0)=1. The posterior-consistency, Gaussian-mixture, concentration, and identifiability results and proofs in Section 3 and Appendix A remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 adds shared local spatial structure as a central explanatory contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. v1 chiefly explained robustness through Bayesian data dominance; v2 presents a joint explanation involving informative measurements and transferable local correlations. The central claim that weak priors can work in informative regimes is retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains reconstruction through measurement anchors and propagation through shared local structure, and suggests that scientific domains may share less transferable structure. It adds high-noise limitations and warns that favorable image-quality metrics can coexist with poorer physics-based performance, motivating task-specific losses. These materially refine applicability and mechanism interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 adds an authors' code-repository link, an explicit exponential-map formula, diagnostic and DRP setup details, and runtime/peak-memory measurements. Existing checkpoint identifiers, hardware, and main hyperparameters remain. The shortened ImageNet description omits v1's explicit validation-split statement, without establishing an actual split change.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and discussion for Deep Random Projector, DAPS, and DiffPIR, broadening comparison with architectural priors and alternative diffusion solvers. Deng et al. and Karras et al. references are removed. Several other changed publication years merely update the same cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution account, Section 3 framing, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around two complementary mechanisms. Section 3 gains separate local-structure and failure discussions, Section 4.4 is condensed, Appendix C is reorganized, and an impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column article to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. v2 adds multiple diagnostic and benchmark tables plus a DRP visualization, and replaces v1's compute curves with Table 17. Most earlier qualitative panels retain their content despite resizing and renumbering; several inaccurate task captions are corrected.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility through stronger baselines and fixed-solver prior-swap controls, addressing v1's limited separation of solver and prior effects. Noise and scientific-imaging tests sharpen failure boundaries, while runtime and memory reporting clarify practical costs. The correlation evidence remains descriptive and some uncertainty details are unspecified, but the gains in validation, transparency, and calibrated guidance outweigh the narrower compute-budget coverage.
